Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent and persistent condition characterized by inattention, impulsivity, and/or hyperactivity. Although current management relies primarily on behavioral assessments and stimulant medication, these existing treatments fail to fully address the disease, driving a growing interest in identifying potential diagnostic biomarkers and developing personalized therapies through neuroimaging. Since child-based resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) is non-invasive, radiation-free, and objective, it serves as an ideal modality for pediatric neurological research. Consequently, this study leverages rs-fMRI scans from 199 children with diagnosed ADHD and 191 typically developing peers to train machine learning algorithms for classification and analysis. We evaluated the overall classification performance of deep neural networks and subsequently isolated crucial brain regions using ablation techniques. Furthermore, we assessed how varying the number of included important regions impacted the network's efficacy. Our investigation revealed that the deep learning model achieved superior results across the entire brain with an accuracy of 73.2% and 73.2% harmonic average, leveraging 79 key regions. Notably, restricting inputs to the most significant 20 regions still yielded comparable performance (68.6% accuracy and 68.4% harmonic average), suggesting these focal areas suffice for robust classification. To address epidemic dynamics, we introduce a distinct-time SISI model where the presence of an infected host is treated as time-specific. In this discrete-time framework, the $\mathit{n}^{th}$ generation represents individuals infected by the host from the $(\mathit{n}-1)^{rd}$ generation, with each generation comprising a Poisson-distributed population size. We establish that a Poisson random field defined on the generation tree for this model yields a unique probability measure and is shown to be analytically equivalent to the Gaussian process from one-class Gaussian process regression, which we name the Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RPH) tree. Additionally, we define an RPH-based branching process and derive its probability of extinction as the Dirichlet distribution; furthermore, our findings indicate this generates the same unique probability measure as observed in the original epidemic model.

This investigation explores current fluctuations within a Klein tunneling interferometer operating within quantum Hall (KH) regimes, using a combined framework of experimental measurements and theoretical modeling. By accessing regimes unattainable in conventional systems, this system reveals that, when subject to asymmetric voltage gradients, a nanodevice operating under KH conditions functions as a switchable thermoelectric generator. The generated power result depends critically on interference patterns, allowing for active control; furthermore, the system's ability to rectify thermal energy flow is demonstrated by connecting two KH edges to a heat source and a electrical lead.

Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) offers substantial promise as a future storage medium due to its exceptional durability and high capacity per unit volume. A proposed DNA arithmetic framework supports efficient retrieval and bulk operations while maintaining data redundancy through forward-error correction via homopolymers. Preserving hierarchical structures within this system facilitates navigable access to multiple data files without reading unnecessary content. Furthermore, robust arithmetic operations necessitate consistent consistency in redundancy levels; consequently, any shift in redundancy information should ideally trigger an automatic hierarchy reorganization to optimize storage. We introduce a novel update mechanism capable of handling changes in both the quantity and position of inserted DNA fragments and detecting inserted homopolymers. Our system design achieves an update efficiency surpassing previous methods by an order of magnitude above current benchmarks while ensuring accurate propagation of hierarchy information and redundancy metadata. Tests conducted at read lengths of up to $10^5$ bp across synthetic datasets of $10^7$ bp demonstrate the system's accuracy and efficacy across diverse scenarios.

This review examines topological phenomena within the macroscopic regimes of condensed matter, electronic, and photonics systems. It begins by outlining various types of nodal points and surfaces in three-dimensional momentum space, along with an explanation of how symmetry protects these features and calculates their topological invariants. The discussion then turns to topological characteristics arising from曲 nodal surfaces, specifically defining theNapier constant and theNodal surfaceCrystalline (EPC) modes. Finally, the paper explores recent experimental work using supercomputers to create and investigate gapped systems with lower dimensions, as well as experiments employing numerous quantum materials such as Weyl and Dirac semimetals, and topological insulators in electronic and photonics contexts.

Pacemaker-generated waves in biological tissues are widely studied using the Newell-Arsenijevic (NA) formulation of the Amplitude Equation (AE), though this approach has seen limited application in deriving analytical solutions for wave velocity. This limitation stems from the Newell-Arsenijevic system being non-autonomous due to time-dependent coefficients, precluding standard techniques for locating travelling wave solutions. Additionally, within a recent paper by the present authors, an autonomous version derived via perturbation has been employed to establish two distinct sets of estimates for wave velocity based on perturbation theory. Here, we apply a method proposed by Kirchg\"{a}ne and Ohadishvili—utilized successfully by Kirchg\"{a}ne for wavefronts in nonlinear wave equations—to generate new, non-perturbative estimates for wave velocity within the NA system. Although these results are technically estimates rather than closed-form analytical values for wave velocity (which remain elusive), they significantly advance tissue dynamics analysis by being non-perturbative and relying solely on pacemaker function and the rate of information dissemination through the wave.

Entropy serves as a foundational measure within information theory and quantum mechanics, though calculating the entropy for arbitrary quantum states is generally intractable. We introduce new fully quantum approaches that estimate the entropy of any efficiently describable quantum state with multiplicative and additive precision in either sublinear or linear time. These algorithms rely on two primary novel contributions: a multiplicative approximation of the quantum trace and a fully quantum implementation of entropy's continuous Hall-Littlewood/spectral type formula. Additionally, we present efficient biparticular separation procedures for quantum systems that can be effectively modeled by Pauli and other sparse operators acting on many qubits.

In the preceding discussion, retrieval and personalization mechanisms within e-commerce platforms were outlined from the perspectives of recommended content and private user area customization. shifting focus, this following section examines the artificial intelligence techniques employed to build such tailored recommendations, alongside their associated technical challenges regarding cloud deployment strategies for service efficiency, data storage duration for content and user metrics, AI processing workflows, return calculation metrics, and revenue generation based on technical and returned product data.

In clinical settings, a physician evaluates a patient's signs and symptoms to formulate a diagnosis. This assessment typically involves three phases: conducting a medical history review by interrogating both the patient and relevant records to identify pertinent issues; performing a physical examination to detect any visible abnormalities; and finally, formulating specific International Classification of Diseases (ICD) diagnostic codes based on findings from the history and examination. To support this workflow, an automated system was developed to assist with ICD classification. By analyzing inputs derived from a patient's history and examination, the system generates the corresponding ICD codes. While currently functional, the examination recognition module was initially built using Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and required thousands of examples to achieve satisfactory performance. To enhance this, a new examination recognizer was created employing Support Vector Machines (SVMs), which significantly improved accuracy with a training dataset of only a few hundred examples. Furthermore, to further boost performance, this study introduces a semi-supervised learning methodology.

Let $R = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the polynomial ring with $n$ variables over a field $k$, and suppose $I$ is a monomial ideal in $R $. A central question in this research area concerns the characterization of monomial ideals $ I $ within $ R $ for which the quotient module $ S = R/I $ is a nearly Cohen-Macaulay structure. In a previous study, the first author presented a sufficient condition for $ R/I $ to possess the nearly Cohen-Macaulay property, leveraging a result by Backelin that expresses any monomial ideal $ I $ as an intersection of primary monomial ideals $ Q_i $ (for $ i=1,\dots,t $) that all share the same projective dimension as $ R/I $. Building upon this framework and a result by Herzog and Vladoiu, the current study establishes the necessity of nearly Cohen-Macaulay conditions for $ R/I $ in relation to these associated quasi-associated $ Q_i $'s.

Machine learning represents a pivotal area within artificial intelligence, aiming to construct robust and efficient systems capable of high-performance data analysis even under conditions of incompleteness or uncertainty. However, extracting maximal insight from vast datasets necessitates the enhancement of user-specific learning algorithms. While neural networks currently serve this purpose widely, they often demand substantial post-processing and extensive training time. Inspired by quantum information theory—specifically the concepts of quantum supervised learning introduced by Knill and Shuai, along with its un supervised variation by Knill—we investigate both versions of these learning algorithms utilizing superconducting quantum hardware. Our results demonstrate superior learning efficiency with quantum approaches compared to their classical counterparts, a superiority further confirmed when these methods are executed on a newly proposed monitored framework and tested on the IBM Quantum Hardware 20-Qubit Superconductors. Monitored quantum learning shows enhanced capabilities across various data scenarios, particularly when compared using metrics such as fidelity or support vector machine kernels.

Guided by the successful detection of the first exoplanoid via the 2015 Kepler mission, the ground-based Wide-field Survey of the Sky for Transient Objects (WIST) was established in 2016. As WIST progressed, the Kepler-Optical Telescope-Network (KMT) survey began in 2017. Both initiatives aim to map the Kepler Field (KF) and equivalent regions across the sky using the 1.3-meter optical/ Near-infrared (O/NIR) instruments located at three strategically placed Chilean observatories to identify transients, the latter being a variable source. As of 2018, the KF has been observed continuously with the 4.8-minute cadence, while the two auxiliary fields (DF8 and DF10) were covered every seven days within a specific timeframe. These observations have yielded thousands of events, which can be categorized into two primary groups: genuine transients and non-transients. This paper details our methodology for classifying anomalies by first removing known variable stars and extraneous sources, followed by an in-depth analysis of the resulting sample to determine the nature and origin of each entry. To address ray casting in inverse problem contexts, we introduce an innovative methodology for determining shadows via shadow rays. The core innovation lies in representing shadows not as binary masks, but as differentiable transmittance functions calculated on shadow planes situated between opaque obstacles and measurement devices. These functions are approximated using neural networks during the obstacle's pixel values, with these networks trained specifically for a particular problem configuration using the obstacles' ground truth labels. The ground truth itself is established by averaging the results of multiple shadow rays originating from random points within the obstacle voxels. This approach yields a computationally efficient solution for shadow calculation that maintains accuracy, even outperforming traditional methods when integrated into inverse problem solvers via its integration of differentiability.

This study introduces a statistical methodology designed to estimate Origin-Destination (OD) demands for specific dates by leveraging daily matrix of traffic links and their average speeds, alongside a single representative day's data. The process begins by estimating time-varying fundamental diagrams (TFDs) through nonparametric regression applied to link speed measurements from one reference day; these TFDs subsequently generate a first approximation of OD demands using daily flow estimates derived from link volumes. To enhance its accuracy, this initial estimation is adjusted via maximum covariance minimization to align with the single day of observed link speeds and, more critically, by integrating uncertainty arising from the simultaneous estimation of both OD demands and fundamental diagrams. When applied to real freeway datasets, this approach demonstrates superior performance in generating speed-based OD estimates for dates distinct from the reference day when compared to methods relying solely on link volume estimates.

While significant insights have been gained regarding the stationary behavior of heterogeneous oscillators—foundational to many biological and physical systems—investigations into their phase-coupling dynamics remain limited. This study introduces a unified framework capable of predicting stationary states as well as traveling and standing waves within extensive arrays of oscillators. By employing an all-encompassing method to map feasible states in both limited and extensive oscillator collections, we clarify the conditions necessary for robust, resistive phase coupling among diverse oscillators.

Uniform spanning trees are a fundamental connection point for random walks on graphs, historically linking through the parallel developments of Wilson's and Aldous-Broder's algorithms. This study theoretically frames these algorithms within a two-phase structure consisting of walk steps and tree steps, driven by a guided tree-building strategy using modified jump rules for selected transitions. By adopting a dynamic model where graph edges are either enabled or disabled based on a predetermined sequence—aligning with recent theoretical work in dynamic graph algorithms—we demonstrate a duality between generalized Wilson's and Aldous-Broder's algorithms on this platform. Specifically, this approach yields a solution-oriented, state-transition-free integration of both algorithms as either individual steps or unified processes of combined execution; at the single walk step level, it produces hybrid algorithms with strictly fewer graph step transitions than the original methods while maintaining asymptotic optimality. Consequently, theoretical predictions regarding the inter-Algorithms and intra-Algorithms efficiencies are validated by simulation studies supported by extensive data.

Although the conversion of sheet music to audio (synthesis) and audio to sheet music to soundings (analysis) are essentially mutual inverse processes, current research treats them as separate challenges, largely due to a lack of datasets featuring both elements alongside ground-truth data. To address this gap, we introduce the MusicTM-Dataset, which unites two previously major but disjoint musical resources: the IMSLP and MTM Databases. These resources contain over 2,000 public domain scores and over 1,000 corresponding audio tracks derived from sheet music created by expert musicians. Prioritizing the robust pairing of scores and audio, this collection represents, according to our analysis, the largest of its kind available to researchers. Leveraging this dataset, we developed a hierarchical multi-task learning model capable of generating musical scores at three distinct levels of notation (standard, reduced, and reduced-two symbols) and the associated audio (timbre) using a unified neural network architecture. Our method yields accurate results across all tasks, as demonstrated by the model's ability to predict scores with higher precision than the existing state-of-the-art methods and the generation of high-fidelity, structured music.

Ontodia provides a runtime environment for querying Knowledge Graphs, where effective visualization and analysis depend significantly on constructing comprehensive knowledge schemas. By integrating schema elements such as classes, properties, domains, ranges, subsets, and conceptual hierarchies, users can retrieve nuanced contextual information; for instance, querying features and related entities for a topic like the "Venetians" yields results distinguishing features present in definitions but not those of "people," alongside hierarchical data comparing "Venetians" to "Italians." Furthermore, direct access to external knowledge sources like Wikidata allows for dynamic and accurate context retrieval, such as locating the precise date of the "St. Mark's Bell Ring" by fetching the month and day of 1452 rather than providing vague ranges. However, knowledge schemas and the contextual data derived from these sources are often incomplete. This study examines two machine learning approaches to automatically enrich both schemas and facts using large-scale text corpora, such as the Wikipedia article text.

Uev is an ongoing prototype designed within an interactive visual analytics research program aimed at managing human workflows during data exploration on functional datasets such as documents or images. This concept is grounded in an emerging methodology that structures session activities as transitions between conceptual 'Lotses'—representations of work states defined by required tasks, activity options, and session flows. So far, Lotev has been manually crafted for specific case studies; however, fully automating its generation by observing user behavior and inferring activity preferences remains a significant challenge. Leveraging this conceptual foundation, researchers are employing Lotev as a unifying framework to organize, consolidate, and release various developed models as modular 'packets.' These components can either curate activity proposals or dictate flow structures and are available via a Visual Analytics Control Panel (VACP integration). Furthermore, these modules are designed for extensive customization or direct extension, allowing developers to override existing packets or inject new analytical capabilities without altering the base concept or other mods.

Optimizing the stellarator's magnetic field is essential for ensuring stable particle confinement and sufficient heating. The example of the conventional H-III-D demonstrates how adjusting coil currents can yield optimal results for magnetic field optimization. With multiple discrete coils, a comprehensive search for the best current configuration is highly beneficial. We present an enhanced version of a coil optimization algorithm designed to simplify such multi-peaked searches. Experimental results show that our method successfully identifies multiple solutions with equivalent quality, including current sets suitable for potential coil removal.

Gas-solid stationary beds are essential across diverse chemical engineering operations, yet understanding three-dimensional (3-D) transport mechanisms within these porous structures remains a significant challenge. In this study, non-invasive and quantitative temperature mappings of a pressurized stationary bed were achieved using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) combined with a Gd₂O₂S:Er dopant for enhanced proton signal emission, all while monitoring for significant line broadening effects. To validate the reliability and precision of the temperature probe and measurement technique, the results were compared against simulations performed on an equivalent idealized porous structure using micro-Computed Tomography (μ-CT). These advanced imaging technologies were then applied to investigate natural convection in a stationary bed containing glass beads with an approximate pore diameter of 140 μm during the top-down dispersion of hot air.

Biomolecular condensates, which form via liquid-liquid phase separation in cells, organize into spatially distinct patterns driven by minimizing free energy. This study demonstrates that when conditions allow a homogeneous bio-molecular system to separate into two phases, an array of such domains can self-assemble on a flat surface shared by multiple condensates. This collective arrays is governed by inter-middle forces, which arise from both direct interactions and a-mediated effects involving an secondary protein. Notably, both direct and indirect forces operate via the same molecular pairs or intermediates involved in the binary coarsening process. Our computational models reveal that this system minimizes its free energy by arranging elements in periodic or quasi-periodic configurations. Furthermore, we observe that condensates positioning at local free energy minima can become entrapped in metastable states. Therefore, our findings indicate that complex self-organization featuring shared components is inherently linked to individual component behavior and provides a framework for building multi-component systems in synthetic biochemical collections.

This paper examines the historical evolution of sunspot numbers and magnetic field strengths for the magnetic region AR 11429, spanning from initial sightings in late 2014 through to 2020. Utilizing comprehensive datasets, including those from the World Data Center for Sunspot spots and contemporary observations, we analyze the development of this magnetic region and its flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) that occurred throughout its lifecycle. Furthermore, the study explores how these solar phenomena influenced geomagnetic disturbances on Earth, specifically through an examination of magnetospheric indices like the Dst index and superstorm indices such as the SSIP index. By correlating sunspot activity indices with these ground-based measurements, we aim to provide a better understanding of the complex interactions between solar eruvers and terrestrial geomagnetic storms. In doing so, the paper contributes to the broader field of space weather forecasting and mitigation strategies against solar-induced space weather events.

Accurate computer simulations of the human heart's mechanical functioning are essential for cardiovascular disease diagnosis, operative planning, and enhancement. Accoringly, robust numerical algorithms with adequate computational efficiency are required to translate theoretical frameworks into applicable tools for diagnosis and improvement of surgical techniques. Algebraic preconditioning is critical for accelerating finite element methods (FEM) to convergence. In this work, a comparative analysis of various scalable multilevel preconditioners is examined using realistic three-dimensional geometries representing operational hearts under various loading states. Preconditioners evaluated in a distributed environment under identical settings are presented, with results indicating that scalable block multitree preconditioners represent promising prospects for heart mechanics application.

Social tagging systems have emerged as a pivotal element of the Web 2.0 architecture; however, assessment of their effectiveness often falters due to an incomplete grasp of user behavior and the complexities of design variations. Drawing upon more than a decade of data from Rybicki, we offer a comprehensive analysis of tagging practices. Our findings reveal that tag reuse constitutes the cornerstone of contributor activity and exhibits distinct patterns contingent on domain and platform features. Additionally, we identify a universal three-phase evolution within emerging topics, characterized by a rapid expansion phase involving exponential label proliferation. Leveraging this insight into interest progression, we introduce the concept of "interest excavation" and explore strategies to harness this dynamic impulse toward enhancing search functionality and promoting content. Finally, through examination of community structures across multiple systems, we explore collaboration phenomena and discuss how these observations can inform the creation of more cohesive user environments.

The continuous advancement of lithographic techniques is a crucial factor driving progress in photonic and acoustic structural research. At the material innovation front, resins capable of withstanding high-intensity laser excitation without degrading now enable micro-precise writing. These robust polymers facilitate the creation of intricate 3D microstructures via direct laser interference patterns, enabling lithographic resolution as fine as 100 nm. Leveraging these capabilities, we have developed a method for fabricating metagrating surfaces on micro-acoustic components resonating at ultra-high frequencies exceeding 1 GHz. Verifying the concept experimentally, we produced dog-bone shaped resonators equipped with metagrating end caps that reached dimensions as small as 500 μm in length and 200 μm in width. Through the precise engineering of gradient features across these surfaces, we achieved deviations in grating reflection of over 90% across ultra-elevated frequency bands exceeding 1000 Hz, surpassing that of conventional gratings by more than tenfold.

This paper investigates the long-term dynamics associated with the 2-D FENE dumbbell model within a compressive fluid framework. A key finding is the establishment of a uniform $L^\infty$ bound for both fluid and molecular variables over this period. Building on this estimate, we demonstrate two distinct asymptotic regimes: first, that the thermal equilibrium state acts as a global attractor in the $L^q$ space (where $1\le q\le 2$); second, that the set comprising both heat equilibrium states and zero-strain-differential-mode solutions constitutes the global robust attractor in the scenario where the first Cauchy–Green strain component remains constant.

The concept of the Integrated Access Backhaul (IAB) was initially introduced within 5G New Air (5GAA) to enable a unified framework for simultaneous access and backhaul communications. Since the Initial Access Committee (IAB) working group later transitioned under Mobile Networks (MN), its scope has been strategically narrowed. While the IAB solution promises to enhance both accessibility throughout the backhaul link, the mobile adaptation of IAB (mIAB) continues to evolve within the mobile network domain. Despite ongoing investigations into the MIB by the IAB panel under MN, numerous technical hurdles remain unaddressed. This paper offers a concise overview of the IAB foundation and explores the challenges specific to mobile integrated access-backhaul (mIAB). Furthermore, it examines the data plane and control interface complexities as well as the MIB feature requirements for mobile scenarios to provide insights into future research directions.

The primary goal of this study is to assess both the efficacy and internal working characteristics of specific hyperparameters commonly used in optimization algorithms, particularly genetic algorithms (GAs), for solving complex, high-dimensional, and non-linear constrained problems. To achieve this, the paper proposes integrating sensitivity analysis into the optimization process itself, thereby enabling simultaneous solution of a multio objective function. This approach allows for calculating parameter efficacy alongside their correlations and interactions with objective function components, as well as their individual variances and joint contributions. By guiding decisions through this comprehensive data, hyperparameter selection becomes significantly more rigorous and scientifically grounded. Furthermore, the proposed methodology offers a tool for analyzing an algorithm's inner workings dynamically during its execution as it progresses toward the final result.

Quantizing single-particle quantum mechanical systems that satisfy specific conditions allows the associated quantum wave equation to be formulated directly in terms of that particle's space-time trajectory (worldline). As a consequence, corresponding physical solutions emerge as asymptotic expansions where each term represents a classical-like trajectory (classical worldline) weighted by an amplitude. This paper utilizes such an asymptonomic structure explicitly calculated in earlier studies to derive various properties regarding asymptomic solutions of the quantum wave equation. Specific assertions include demonstrating that these solutions possess well-defined probability current distributions exhibiting classical diffusion; showing that probability density ratios across different locations approximate the ratio of their associated classical line integrals; proving that solutions accurately replicate classical dynamics when applied to multi-body systems; and establishing that asymptotic solutions effectively quantify single-particle phenomena such as virtual particles, pair production, and pair annihilation.

Current reinforcement learning (RL) agents often struggle due to environments that are too complex for effective learning. While simulation tests using synthetic tasks support their development, they lack the ecological validity required for reliable generalization evaluations, as opposed to real-world settings. To address this gap, we introduce L2Explorer—a comprehensive ecosystem comprising 225 distinct real-world and simulated tasks across domains such as navigation, manipulation, and strategy. This collection spans varying degrees of simulation fidelity and includes integrated methods for simulating interference and social interference to evaluate robustness. We describe the composition of L2Explorer and analyze the performance of four prominent RL agents across all tasks, identifying environmental factors that influence agent success. Ultimately, we propose future enhancements to L2Explorer to better accelerate RL development.

At Keck Observatory, the Light and Ray-Trace Imaging and Spectroscopy (Liger) instrument represents the first new addition in nearly twenty years. As a flexible digital camera capable of both visual/spectroscopic capabilities during the day and infrared imaging at night, Liger serves both supporting functions for the existing Infrared Instrument/Imagers Spectrograph (II/N) and as a primary instrument at the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLI). Given its dual-mode function, Liger plays a vital role in combined data acquisition alongside VLI operations. Developed by the National Optical-Infrared Observatory (NOIRL) Project, this system marks the centerpiece of the Submillimeter Wave Instrument (SMWI) project, which aims to introduce three advanced instruments to NOIRL by 2025. Because Liger currently provides essential monitoring for VLI activities, its successful integration is essential for future combined data analysis projects. This paper outlines the data processing framework designed to handle concurrent Liger and VLI operations as well as interference control tasks, emphasizing Liger's critical role within that broader workflow, which will eventually include real-time data analysis pipelines.

This paper introduces a new class of stochastic all-or-none wave solutions arising from two-dimensional, non-laminar, and time-independent flow of viscous materials described by the Navier-Stokes equations. This paper introduces a report on experiments involving retina image analysis utilizing deep neural networks (DNNs), targeting the classification of healthy eyes along with categories of glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy. This paper explores an innovative approach to identifying features of COVID-19 ICU admissions through digital analysis of chest X-rays, utilizing a Brazilian dataset. Detecting visual concepts within natural scenes is a fundamental challenge in computer vision, recently enhanced by powerful trained models like object detectors and visual encoders when paired with reliable training data. However, two primary issues persist: first, trained architectures often struggle with generalization due to biases toward frequent classes; second, reliable data sets frequently contain annotation errors that generate false positives, particularly for subtle concepts, compromising downstream performance. Extracting the social relationships of public figures is essential for building knowledge networks used in tasks such as disambiguation, identity verification, profiling, and creating biographical summaries. To effectively handle this complexity, we introduce **NetRel**, a unified architecture that transforms unstructured text into social relation graphs. Although similar to generic relation extraction models, netrel is adapted from scratch to specifically capture the intricate nuances of social interactions. We evaluated its performance against human-constructed gold standards using two distinct datasets, where it achieved the second-highest accuracy for low-resource languages and the second-highest accuracy for large-scale datasets respectively; furthermore, we profiled the system to demonstrate that its generalization capabilities stem from three sources: its specialized parameters tailored to social relations, its adaptation to raw unstructured data, and its integration with pre-trained transformer knowledge.

Although identity recognition research has largely shifted focus to natural images, the visual analysis of surveillance footage depicting crowded scenes offers a more difficult yet practically important challenge. To address this, we propose a framework capable of simultaneously locating and identifying all individuals within an image, introducing a new system called DGMTNet built on dynamic graph message transmission layers designed to model long-range dependencies across the whole scene. First, specialized sub networks utilizing these layers extract contextual features from potential person instances detected by prior algorithms. Following extraction, the system applies a self-loop based on a proposed distance hypothesis specific to person detection. Finally, the framework integrates designed correlation modules to refine the initial detection outputs and effectively links potential person candidates. Evaluated against challenging image datasets containing complex background difficulties and dense populations, respectively, results demonstrate improvements of over 10% and 5% in accuracy compared to two state-of-the-art methods, ultimately proving both its effectiveness and practical utility.

Hyper spectral imaging offers numerous advantages within autonomous driving domains. These findings underscore that rocky planet formation involves multiple pathways, all potentially capable of accounting for observed alignment statistics.

Achieving versatile object manipulation, such as firmly grasping, is a pivotal yet unresolved challenge in current gripper engineering. Achieving this consistency often requires complex physical control strategies that drive closed-loop mechanisms with high backdriveability to ensure a secure hold on soft materials. Furthermore, accurately predicting the force exerted by these soft grippers remains difficult due to their inherent nonlinearity and the high dependency of force on deformation. Conversely, analyzing the deformation itself is complex because it relies on accurate finite element modeling of both the structural properties and the non-linear hyperelastic interactions between the soft fingers and object surfaces. To address these hurdles, this study leverages recent developments in Koopman operator-based modeling. We introduce an efficient virtual modeling and regulation framework tailored for soft grippers using air-actuated designs with multiple fingers. By utilizing experimental data to build data-driven, nonlinear dynamical models via coordinate transformation into a nearly low-dimensional space using the discrete time-time-separated (DT-TBT) algorithm, we achieve precise force estimation and the synthesis of specific input trajectories for virtual control schemes. Validation through both simulation and physical experiments demonstrates that the proposed method produces dynamical representations that align closely with actual system behaviors, resulting in highly accurate force estimates and successful formation control when compared against real-world results.

Gradient Descent (GD), the prevailing approach for optimizing neural networks, has spurred recent theoretical efforts elucidating its convergence mechanisms. A critical area of research involves understanding how this algorithm leverages network over-parameterization to identify minimal solutions within highly fragmented loss landscapes. Recent theoretical advancements have demonstrated that when faced with a discrete landscape, standard neural networks equipped with tangent attention layers can achieve minimization of a surrogate continuous loss function through gradient descent, thereby facilitating proof of GD's convergence in nonsmooth landscapes. Building on these insights, this work investigates the extension of this phenomenon to cases where the loss landscape involves a discrete product structure.

Radio sources in distant galaxies offer valuable insight into the early development of black holes and stars. This study presents high-resolution observations of the radio lobe system J2102+6015, which recently underwent a jet-powered explosion at an redshift of 4.575. Evidence for this dynamic history includes bright emission from the shock front surrounding the lobes, radio brightness symmetry, and morphological signs of deceleration within the expanding fuel. Furthermore, data reveals a V-shaped structure of counterlobes extending toward the center, indicative of past lobe expansion driven by an ejecta stream that has since largely dissipated. By analyzing the spectrum and morphology, researchers conclude that the driving supersonic jet was roughly 0.3 parsecs long and roughly balanced in brightness with the visible lobes. Such distant, jet-activated lobes represent a rare phenomenon, making J2102+6015 a critical benchmark for investigating the coupled evolution of supermassive black holes and their stellar galactic hosts.

Lung cancer ranks as both the most prevalent malignancy and the primary cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Despite advances in diagnosis and treatment, progress in reducing incidence rates and mortality remains limited due to prolonged timelines for new discoveries. Consequently, identifying innovative lung carcinoma (NSCLC) cases is crucial for enhancing patient outcomes and controlling mortality rates over time. Finally, we conducted a comprehensive experimental evaluation on a substantial dataset of 40,000 images to verify the proposed framework's efficacy, demonstrating significant improvements in AUC scores alongside rapid convergence.

Twitter Sentiment Assessment (TSA) has become a critical area of study in Social Media Mining (SMM) due to the explosive growth of user-generated content on platforms like Twitter. Conversational Artificial Intelligence is a rapidly growing research domain driven by recent advances in large-scale language models, which have shifted focus toward enhancing model usability and coherence within specific dialogue contexts. While current approaches often assign conversation roles simply by injecting few-shot examples into prompt contexts—a method constrained by limited few-shot data that fails to fully leverage pre-trained knowledge—this study addresses the challenge of role definition using only a static set of fixed functional terms provided by the language model. We introduce a framework built on a pre-trained language model that encages functional roles within a unified continuous semantic space. This approach represents each role with specific functional terms and individual roles using fewer than a handful of selected terms. We define this framework through two primary research questions: first, examining how effectively various functional terms generate distinct and comprehensive representations for different conversations, and second, assessing the utility of a role-specific continuous space for representing individual dialogue actions. Experimental evaluations across a spectrum of large-scale language models demonstrate that our proposed framework identifies functional terms capable of achieving a high degree of inter-role distinction and establishes a robust foundation for modeling fine-grained user interactions. Furthermore, our results indicate that employing this continuous space representing individual users significantly enhances the quality of generated dialogue compared to baseline methods.

We demonstrate that electron-light interactions maintain measure invariance regarding both time and space within mesoscopic systems by analyzing first-principles-derived tight-binding models. This finding implies that deriving expectation values for physical observables remains consistent whether calculated using time-independent or time-dependent probability distributions, thereby confirming the robustness of standard time-independent quantum mechanics in such environments. Semantic keypoints represent an innovative approach to semantics-rich image encoding, yet they also present significant challenges for models aiming to infer both 3D object pose and 2-3D shape. To address this, we introduce a novel category-aware loss function designed to optimize the estimation of object pose and shape simultaneously with semantic keypoints. Since semantic keypoints for a specific object category can vary slightly based on their appearance or scene context, we propose generating these keypoints via an image-conditional encoder via a separate module. Furthermore, we formulate this learning process as an "ideal" optimization task and extend the method to "resilient" scenarios capable of handling noisy keypoints. Markedly, our technique yields substantial performance gains across the demanding tasks of category-aware 3D object localization and category-aware 3D shape recovery when evaluated against existing baseries on the HumAin3D and COCO-3D datasets.

basket trials are increasingly utilized in drug development to evaluate spatially or temporally separated patient groups believed to share a common pathological mechanism, often allowing reduced sample sizes through design efficiencies. While current methods for sample size determination in these trials generally ignore the random effect correlations, this paper proposes an approach that factors in the impact of basket level correlation to estimate sample numbers for both equal and unequal allocation scenarios. These novel methods, implemented via both simple analytical formulas and computational algorithms, account for various trial designs, including those without a control group or using two arms per basket, as well as situations with multiple subsets per basket. The industry leading in motion dynamics, such as semiconductor and semiconductor manufacturing, is increasingly demanding greater precision and performance. To achieve these standards, many specialized industries utilize motor-driven mechanisms to position items within their operations. Enhancing position resolution remains a critical focus for various sectors striving for improved product quality. This study introduces a novel control strategy designed to elevate the trajectory fidelity of motor-systems. Drawing inspiration from high-precision platforms like optical line profile systems (LPV-SLS), our method implements a line-following algorithm that integrates two distinct loops: a shuttle loop managing system movement during transitions between line segments, and a non-shuttle loop responsible for precise position tracking while the act moves. Our theoretical analysis reveals that although both loops contribute to positioning resolution, the non-shuttle loop assumes a primary role regarding accuracy, effectively becoming the dominant factor determining the result. Furthermore, a theoretical model predicts resolution based on loop dynamics and system parameters; we validate this theory through simulations based on an actual implementation focused on high-power laser delivery for semiconductor marking.

Achieving precise image registration across various fields has proven vital for applications ranging from medical diagnostics to military targeting. However, manually creating registration pairs is often labor-intensive, prompting a shift toward leveraging vast libraries of unlabeled images to train registration models. Unsupervised learning from unlabeled data for image alignment has thus garnered significant research attention. While numerous methods have emerged focusing fully on fully supervised learning using unlabeled data, this work introduces PRNet, a novel approach for aligning images with unlabeled data for partial overlap. Specifically, PRNet employs a cost function that facilitates the learning of cross-partial partial overlap. The proposed method has proven capable with unsupervised training, successfully aligning images that do not have to be in full overlap previously, thus proving to be an effective tool. Testing demonstrates PRNet's performance surpasses that of self-supervised methods, as well as being more efficient in the P2-1.5D and full-supervised settings. Furthermore, our method has proven particularly useful in the medical field, allowing us to extract useful structural information from single CT scans to enhance diagnostic capabilities.

Small-world networks are defined by a low average path (diameter) between nodes, representing compact topologies often found in social structures and internet protocols, making them vital for large-scale learning and inference. A primary challenge in these environments is estimating the network's scale—specifically its diameter—which is essential for configuring various data-driven tasks. This paper addresses the problem of estimating the diameter in large, arbitrary small-world graphs influenced by Byzantine errors, utilizing estimation methods robust against corrupted inputs. Note that standard non-robust "vote-and-count" techniques can be significantly skewed by adversarial nodes; consequently, this study introduces and analyzes the "Byzantine-perturbed Random Walk (BRW)" mechanism, an strategy that maintains accurate diameter estimation even when attacked. Under the assumption that the majority of nodes possess local view knowledge, an $O(D)$-time algorithm is used to estimate the true diameter $D$ via BRW with a multiplicative error bound of $(1\pm\epsilon)$ using $O(N\cdot D^2/\epsilon^2)$ Byzantine-perturbed walks ($N$ being the total node count). When applied exclusively to small-world graphs, this algorithm achieves both a $\tilde{O}(N)$ execution time and a space requirement of $\tilde{O}(N)$ (where $\tilde{O}$ suppresses polylogarithmic factors), all while remaining resistant to Byzantine attacks.

Federated Learning (FL) functions as a distributed machine learning approach where multiple clients train local models on their own data and transmit the resulting model updates to a central server for aggregation, thereby preserving local data privacy entirely within each client's environment. This work presents high-resolution optical and near-infrared imaging of UGC 8839, a low-mass, early-type spiral galaxy, captured by the VLT/UVES Integral Field Unit (IFU). Generating nonlinear optical phenomena like high-order harmonic generation (HHG) involves splitting a pulsed infrared laser into a brief extreme ultraviolet/soft extreme ultraviolet (XUV) pulse and an attenuated infrared remnant. A critical objective is to maximize the XUV pulse fluence while preserving significant fluence in the infrared carrier wave. However, conventional setups typically exhibit poor fluence stability and broad spectral bandwidths, which hinder optimal conversion ratios. This study introduces a new approach called "chirp-tapering." It uses a femtosecond pulse shaper to simultaneously apply both negative amplitude and frequency chirps to the initial pump pulse. This technique temporally stretches the already broadened pump pulse during propagation, thereby concentrating the complex conjugate field toward the center of the pulse. Consequently, when this shaped and stretched pulse interacts with the focus point during harmonic generation, a tapered intensity profile is created instead, significantly boosting overall efficiency. Using a numerically simulated CGS gas-filled setup with a 500 as pulse width at 25 mJ energy, this method increased peak harmonic fluence by a factor of 177 compared to a standard Gaussian pump. By optimizing parameters such as taper depth and relative phase, researchers can achieve arbitrary control over the resulting harmonic spectrum.

Identifying defects in textile production is critical to the industry, yet current manual inspection methods are labor-intensive, inefficient, and prone to error. Our goal was to leverage human visual system characteristics, specifically sensitivity to irregularities, in order to enhance Luminance image quality and simultaneously pinpoint flaw locations. We proposed a novel approach involving the calculation of Human Visual System-based Gradient Directional Octagon (HVS-GDGO) features from original images to capture directional information crucial for pattern recognition. These features were used to construct feature maps, which demonstrate that patterns appear as uniform white areas while anomalies stand out as black spots, facilitating instant visual interpretation by humans and machines alike. Furthermore, a matrix construction technique was implemented to translate image data into an easily comprehensible format using low-rank decomposition, effectively eliminating ambiguity. Experimental findings confirm that this proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art flaw detection approaches.

We propose a data-theoretic regularization framework designed to enhance deep reinforcement learning-based visual navigation agents. As key applications, we demonstrate its utility in both offline reinforcement learning with offline datasets online exploring using simulated environments. Using entropy regularizers as a case example, we show that incorporating log-determinant of feature covariance not only matches the offline performance of standard KL regularizers but also improves online learning. For both tasks, our approach achieves SOTA results with a simpler architecture. We also demonstrate that with smaller datasets, our method yields significantly better performance gains.

We present a numerical investigation into gravitational waves generated by binary star systems within galactic nuclei. Our model accounts for both secular and dynamical interactions during binary-hard stellar encounters, utilizing Monte Carlo simulations to explore various population synthesis scenarios. By varying parameters such as the mass ratio of binaries, the star formation timescale, and the rate at which binaries gain mass through interactions, we analyze how these factors influence orbital evolution and wave emission spectra, specifically looking at wave amplitudes versus chirp mass and orbital frequency distributions. We examine systems interacting with stars of uniform mass as well as scenarios involving a metallic background mass distribution. Although numerical results indicate that binaries typically merge within a Hubble time following their final structural adjustments, we identify specific parameter sets where large eccentricities are retained until the point of merger, significantly boosting gravitational wave amplitudes. We conclude by comparing our derived spectral signatures against observational data.

In the face of escalating demand for electricity caused by population growth and rising living standards, power supply has struggled to keep pace, necessitating a focus on supply-side solutions. Consequently, energy conservation through intelligent usage monitoring and control has become a critical strategy for meeting surging needs for 电力. sensor-based monitoring systems, capable of assessing performance across diverse appliances and infrastructure components, are essential for effective management. However, the primary obstacle lies in the inability of these sensors to directly measure flow variables, such as current and voltage, preventing straightforward data interpretation. To address this challenge, we present a comprehensive framework utilizing parameter estimation techniques to infer such flows from available sensor data. Multiple estimation methods are employed, leveraging both sparse data and rich information regarding the network's topology to aid calculation. Experimental validation using data from a realistic simulation of a residential street demonstrates that the proposed approach effectively reconstructs flow dynamics and simultaneously identifies events based on these structures.

This study investigates the decay channels $X(3872)\rightarrow J/\psi \pi\gamma$ and $X(3872)\rightarrow J/\psi \pi\pi\delta$ within the framework of hadronic molecular models. By applying a newly developed analytical formula, we compute numerically both form factors $g_Q^Q(\qi)$ and $g_Q^Q(\qi)$ for $i=\pi,\delta$ and $Q=\pi,\sigma$, accounting for finite size effects on the form factors. Our numerical calculations demonstrate that accounting for finite particle sizes significantly alters the linearly $Q^Q$ dependent form factors. While decay rates derived from the effective point-like approximation show qualitative alignment with experimental observations when integrating finite size corrections, we conclude that incorporating this finite size is essential for achieving precise matching between theoretical decay rates and experimental data.

While Caviglia's work provides categorical descriptiosn of the Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre cohomology for extensions involving linear algebraic groups whose quotient is finite and for unipotent extensions, this paper extends those results to the context of quad Morita descriptors. Specifically, we consider finite quadratics and formally trivial and extension of quadratics. We demonstrate that under quadratics morphism, the Lyndon-Hochschild-Serge cohomology is faithful through the description using quad Morita descriptors, extending the results mentioned above to the broader category.

Text-based games present remarkable difficulty for both computer agents and humans due to slow information retrieval rates, forcing interactions at approximately ten moves per second. To address this bottleneck, we introduce TextWorldExpress, a virtual emulation environment optimized for high-speed simulation achieving approximately 30,000 times a faster interaction rate. This advancement allows essential world-state updates to occur in bulk during batch processing rather than individually. As demonstrated by its application, this text-game specific acceleration significantly enhances world exploration efficacy for evaluating and assessing artificial intelligence performance.

We present an "approximate-geometric" framework to derive effective Hamiltonians for topological insulators of all spin charges $ \text{2D/3D} $, accounting for generic defects, which include deviations from periodicity, disorder, and flaws. Using this approach derived from an approximated spectrum of a discrete Schrödinger (or Dirac/Fermi) equation, we construct a general perturbation scheme for topological quasicrystalline systems in quasisolid-state physics. The method yields effective Hamiltonians for low-energy states expressed via spatial polynomials of $ s $-th order (for $ s\geq 2 $), wherein coefficients depend critically on defect characteristics. Specifically, we analyze defects modeled as random structures of different dimensions: 0D impurities, 1D vortices/walls, and 2B Bloch points. The derived Hamiltonians facilitate a rigorous study of density of states (DoS) scaling with system size, $g_c(L)$, demonstrating its universality across various defects within each class of TIs, while also determining effective g-factors for these quasisubbands via Landau-Lifshits theory. This approach enables quantification of defect-induced shifts in energy levels relative to perfect bands.

This paper explores $p$-harmonic functions within two-dimensional sectors through explicit formulas, assessing both their asymptotic behaviors at infinity and their bounds relative to powers of the radial coordinate. The study concludes by examining when powers of the radial function, $x^m=V(x)^p$, satisfy $p$-harmonicity. The methods and analysis presented rely primarily on the theory of $p$-harmonic measure, which was developed by the authors previously [math.CA/06064600].

This study introduces a method to generate conditionally extreme multivariate spatial peaks of significant waves, preserving the original peak periods and spatial distribution characteristics. A spatial extreme value model, grounded in the Anderson-Wheatley framework and adapted throughEWL marginal distributions, provides an efficient approach to simulate these unprecedented significant wave heights under specific spatial peak locations. While marginal distributions have previously been examined, this research evaluates the approach further through additional marginal analyses, along with spatial and temporal-spatial dependency checks. This work adds to the literature by applying the Anderson-Wheatley model to extreme wave data for the first time. Results confirm that the proposed method effectively captures dependence structures across different scales, offering valuable conditions and insights for potentially worse sea states.

This paper presents a technique for synchronizing the realms of manipulability through bilateral manipulation within human-robot collaborative settings, a capability that extends robot tools under human guidance by aligning their respective operational domains. Experimental validation using an iCub humanoid robot and a YASKAWA robot arm demonstrates accurate realm adjustment, quantified by a 30.45% average enhancement in manipulability volume.

Reinforcement learning has proven highly effective at task-specific learning, yet generalizing across unrelated tasks remains difficult. To test this generalization across domains, we introduce the concept of "unintentional tasks"—goals implied by task descriptions but not explicitly defined for success. We present the environment "Corridor3D," featuring agents in a 3D setting who must sort and stack shapes according to color while the agent description vaguely suggests optimizing 3D positioning as an auxiliary goal. Although color categorization lacks any mentioned connection to 3D placement, the color 2D learning agent generalizes to this implicit 3D objective. We evaluate this system by cross-correlating 3D positions with the color camera feed to build a method for learning in unseen scenarios using sparse observation data and a straightforward color-to-3D suggestion.

Infodemics are accelerating globally, causing significant harm as people accept false information rather than reliable data. This impact extends further when misinformation propagates within familial networks, potentially undermining efforts to control severe outbreaks like COVID-19 by delaying necessary vaccinations. Consequently, there is an urgent requirement to monitor misinformational activities within families and interfere before such narratives are internalized or rejected as false within those close circles. Recent technological advancements offer hope, enabling the automatic classification of misinformation using digital footprints like social media interactions. Specifically, Twitter provides a vast repository of discourse surrounding misinformation topics, where users often initiate claims that others either support or contest through retweets or unfrets. Since the acceptance or rejection of false claims significantly influences belief formation, this study proposes a method to automatically determine the intended stance of Twitter authors regarding misinformational posts related to vaccine skepticism. By analyzing Unstructured sentences drawn from Twitter into organized groups through topic modeling, researchers applied supervised learning techniques to create an effective binary classifier. The results indicate a strong performance with an F1-score reaching 0.86999, demonstrating that such technological capabilities can empower individuals, families, and misinformational campaigns to mitigate the spread of false claims during critical public health emergencies.

Generating isolated attosecond pulses is vital for probing ultrafast electron motion within materials, yet prior efforts have fallen short due to the typically large pulse energy required for creation, which hinders sensitivity to minor temporal shifts. We introduce a method producing attosecond surge radiation with reduced energy demands while maintaining simple three-laser setups using a new coherent radiation generation strategy that uses counter-rotating circular fields instead of a three-phase approach. This allows for better control over field dynamics leading to improved signal quality and lower energy output compared to traditional techniques in creating attosecond bursts.

We examine the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation within a bounded domain featuring a convex barrier, subject to the Dirichlet boundary condition, focusing on local solutions that exist near their eigenfunctions. A primary contribution of this work is an existence theorem for explosion-type solutions in scenarios where local solutions exist near their eigenfunctions and blow up in a specific manner as the parameter approaches a critical threshold from a particular direction. Furthermore, under specific additional conditions, we establish the equivalence between an explosion solution's existence and non-existence, respectively, and their blow-up at the boundary versus within the interior of the domain.

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a promising framework for solving differential equations by merging deep learning capabilities with knowledge of physical laws. Despite their potential, standard PINNs face critical limitations: they struggle with adaptive local refinement of variables, require extensive training time, and demand extensive data on boundary and initial conditions. To address these issues, this paper introduces Residual-driven Adaptive Node Generation (RAN), a novel node-ablation technique designed to enhance the efficiency and convergence of PINNs. RAN operates by dynamically inserting virtual neural network data in areas exhibiting high prediction errors, effectively performing local adaptive refinement. By reducing the size of training batches during these ablations, RANG concentrates computational power within zones of error, thereby improving solution convergence significantly. Experimental results across the heat equation, an Unsteady State Advection-Diffusion equation, and the Barometric formula demonstrate that RAN outperforms conventional full-batch training in saving training time while delivering equally accurate solutions.

Multi-domain superlattices within ferroelectric FETs (FeFETs) exhibit a distinctive hysteresis loop featuring a narrower capacitance narrowing compared to single-domain structures, a phenomenon attributed to the specific morphology of domains. To investigate this three-pointbend FeFET model, which operates on domain walls confined to the electrostatic $1/4$ and $1/2$ positions, we built upon a previously established finite-element-based simulation framework. Our results confirm that these well-defined domain wall positions allow for the analytical prediction of experimental hysteresis loops by integrating the effects with superlattices of dielectric materials positioned atop the channel.

Recently, supply chain networks have become targets for disruptions originating from the novel coronavirus. As a backbone sector, the freight industry ensures food and medicine are accessible and supports dependent industries, such as agriculture, pharmaceuticals, and manufacturing. The study aims to utilize complex system analysis to uncover hidden vulnerabilities within these interconnected structures. First, a multi-sector dependency graph was constructed using public sources, including the 2012 U.S. Input-Output Database and the Federal Highway Administration's Freight Demand Survey. Next, the research introduced a novel network metric called "fragniture," designed specifically to quantify the potential spread of supply chain fractures. Finally, the developed fragniture index was applied to identify the most fragile supply chains, offering stakeholders crucial knowledge to enhance the resilience of the broader transportation system.

This study addresses an stochastically driven intricate Bingham-Hand equations and includes a pure-type jump noise component. We are able to demonstrate that the corresponding Markov process exhibits irreducibility, possesses a unique invariant measure which is both stationary and ergodic, and finally we are able to conclude strong asymptotic stability in the mean square convergence under the specified conditions where the stationary distributions converge to zero. We are able to show some special cases such as when there is no noise influence at all, we can recover some known results about unique invariant measures under strong assumptions regarding the potential function's lower bounds.

This paper determines the $k$-degree of the power graph for all finite nilpotent groups and finite abelian groups that possess the largest cyclic subgroup. A graph is $k$-degred if every induced subgraph with more than $k$ vertices is not complete, yet the original graph itself remains incomplete. We establish the conditions defining such graphs and a set of twenty-one open problems related to them. In doing so, we also define and examine $L$-degeneration, a property present in all abelian groups of rank less than or equal to two.

This paper presents an analysis of scalar orientation networks (SCORN) and their application to classification. We propose Scalar Convolution Layer (SCACLs), orientational components designed for vector-valued convolutional neural networks, enabling the representation of tensor-valued orientations. These layers facilitate efficient, element-wise operations on vectorvalued orientation tensors through a compact architecture. We demonstrate these models are adaptable, achieving top-tier performance on several standard image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and MNIST. Additionally, our work extends these networks with logarithmic mapping components, enhancing data-eficient learning by incorporating knowledge transfer mechanisms.

Point cloud segmentation is crucial for understanding scene contents, yet it remains difficult due to complex structures and irregular surface point distributions. Although recent neural networks based on graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have achieved significant success in using regularizations to handle surface irregularities, their performance on point clouds is suboptical when compared to their success with images and volumes. This study investigates these limitations and introduces new GCN-based advancements including: (1) a novel graph learning method that constructs more appropriate relationships between points; (2) a multi-scale modeling strategy designed to enhance segmentation on medium-resolution maps, commonly found in driving scenarios; (3) a modeling approach that efficiently integrates side-information, such as color, into the graphs; (4) a specialized model tailored specifically for road segmentation tasks. Experiments validate that our proposed methods yield notable improvements across various challenges, resolutions, and datasets, including the driving-oriented AutoDrive test set. This work investigates carbon-carbon fusion by highlighting recent experimental findings alongside theoretical calculations. Since the early 1980s, observations have revealed an anomaly outside the traditional barrier region in ${}^{12}{\rm C}+{}^{12}{\rm C}$ reactions; specifically, reaction cross sections significantly exceed predictions based on optical model theory alone. Addressing this discrepancy, our study employs the promising Trojan Horse Scenario (THT) to perform reaction cross section measurements at ultra-low energies. These new data points, combined with the most rigorous theoretical models to date, have established that THT offers an excellent fit for explaining the fusion process within the sub-barrier regime. We conclude this report by examining the significant relationship between ultra-low energy nucleosynthesis rates and the precision derived through the Trojan Horse Method in such environments.

The widespread adoption of mobile devices has rendered conventional indoor localization methods, reliant on GPS, impractical. Consequently, wireless positioning techniques exploiting Channel State Information (CSI) from Wireless Local Area Networks (WLANs) serve as a viable alternative for locating devices within mobile networks. Although multiple studies demonstrate the potential of using modulation-coding-variant CSI profiles—distinct from traditional received signal strength—for positioning, this research highlights an underexplored issue: significant fluctuations ("jitter") in CSI that complicate accurate user equipment localization. To mitigate this noise, we introduce an efficient algorithmic correction to such variations, followed by our proposed A2-Attention system. This framework leverages deep neural networks to restore distorted CSI data, thereby boosting position estimation accuracy. Experimental validation using a real-world dataset confirms that A2-attention outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, cutting relative error by approximately 18%.

Computational systems biology modeling is a highly intricate and constantly evolving domain; consequently, modeling software must adapt to keep pace with these advancements to effectively harness the field's increasing capability. Current landscape analysis reveals two distinct categories of tools to manage data and models. The first consists of simple, lightweight interfaces suited for basic tasks. The second group comprises heavy-duty, comprehensive platforms capable of handling complex workflows. At the extremes, lightweight tools often lack sufficient functionality, while comprehensive platforms are overwhelmed with options that distract users focusing on specific tasks. To bridge this divide between simplicity and complexity, we introduce an innovative concept within systems biology: a front-end application designed to connect user-specific inputs into standard COPASI models. This interface allows users to modify models by entering custom data points rather than configuring detailed settings. Easing development barriers, the application can utilize existing code written in Shiny, a user-friendly language suitable for general users. The outcome is an intuitive bridge that guides even novice users.
ShinyCOPASI unifies model interaction into an efficient workflow without sacrificing simplicity. Users can interactively upload and manipulate data, such as curves and tables, to enhance their research exploration. The interface automatically generates corresponding graphs based on curve-fitting results for seamless analysis. The interface offers significant usability advantages, including the ability to create tailored applications based on specific needs or distinct datasets, all driven by the user-friendly ShinyCOPASI tool.

In Science and Technology for Information (STEM) fields, there has been an increasing emphasis on integrating machines and algorithms to interpret graphs, tables, and other forms of data visualization. While existing systems have made progress in areas such as set interpretation and question answering, their ability to deliver explainable answers and insights within the visual interpretation community remains limited. Existing solutions tend to offer only local explanations focused on specific inputs, lacking a consistent framework for quantifying ambiguity regarding particular data points or answers.

We introduce an extensive framework capable of measuring ambiguity at both individual and systemic levels, supported by diverse methodologies including clustering, set coverage, and neural networks. We evaluate 14 state-of-the-art models across several datasets to assess their performance. Among the tested approaches, Random Forest emerged as the least ambiguous system, with Set and Cluster Cover demonstrating strong results in reducing ambiguity through Set interpretations.

Findings indicate that Set is a more reliable method for generating meaningful explanations than the currently used Cluster method. Furthermore, we identified several valid types of valid explanations and established metrics to gauge the reliability of these explanations within explanation systems.

The authors introduce and examine an operator algebra consisting of convolution operators linked to functions within the category of the commutant of the canonical representation on a compact quantum group. In several instances, they establish that this algebra forms a von Neumann type I.

Iterative methods are frequently employed to approximate the value function within finite Markov decision processes (MDPs), particularly when their state space is so vast that it precludes closed-form analytical solutions. Building upon prior extensive MDP frameworks where transition likelihoods and environmental dynamics are described using tabular formats capable of holding an infinite number of states, we introduce a generalized implicit GMRES iteration designed to facilitate applied approximate dynamic programming. We provide theoretical convergence analyses for both standard and sample-efficient variants of this method, demonstrating convergence in exact precision relative to effective communication complexity and in sample count relative to both squared impulse variation and square-root sampling costs per unit time. Furthermore, we illustrate that our approach substantially surpasses full gradient descent from full Hessian matrix iterations in terms of computational sample-efficiency, while also demonstrating superior theoretical convergence rates compared to existing approximate dynamic programming strategies tailored for extensive MDP environments comprising continuous or highly discretized state spaces that cannot be fully explored through exhaustive queries or deterministic updates.

This study introduces a novel approach to calibrate a dynamic, time-series-valued computational model with unknown parameters using a Multiple Contour Assessment framework designed for global optimization. The method addresses the substantial challenge posed by high dimensionality within global optimization algorithms, particularly those reliant on probabilistic scoring of candidate solutions, by implementing an effective dimensionality reduction technique dependent on continuous dimension analysis. This technique reduces the search space based on continuous contour theory through low dimensional embedding while preserving key structural characteristics of the data. During each optimization iteration, the search space is projected onto a projected subspace constructed via a supervised learning algorithm tailored to identify the most discriminating features of the data. Specifically, the search space is mapped onto a projected subspace by selecting a subset of features derived from the time series that retain the distinguishing variations between different datasets. During each iteration these dimensions are chosen adaptively according to how the search space evolves, based on comparisons between simulated model outputs and real observed time series values used for testing purposes.
